title: Mac: one row per device in Devices, and file-receive acks that actually route back to Linux senders
highlights: Mac: Devices now shows a single, canonical row per physical peer no matter how many identifiers it has been seen under. The identity model is explicit — canonical `id` is the peer's UUID when known (TXT `id` or first Hello), Bonjour name as a fallback — and each `Device` carries an `aliases` set, so the old name-keyed row and the new UUID-keyed row of the same peer collapse the moment the first Hello arrives. Pre-0.1.60 trust records (which only had a Bonjour name) decode cleanly and survive the upgrade without re-pairing. Two distinct devices that happen to share a Bonjour hostname stay as two rows.

Mac: `FileTransferService` ack routing is fixed for Linux senders. Previously the Mac routed `fileAck` back by `envelope.senderDeviceId` (the sender's UUID), but the Mac's outbound map was keyed by the dialed Bonjour name — the lookup missed and the ack was silently dropped, so the Linux sender timed out waiting for chunk 0. Acks now go out on the exact transport that delivered the chunk (threaded through as a `replyToken`), with the peer-id path kept as a fallback. Transfers originating from Linux peers that the Mac never dialed itself now complete.

Mac: the Devices row got a tighter layout. Name is bold on top; subtitle is `<platform> · Trusted/Not trusted · <version>`. Four capability icons line up on the right — Trust, Keyboard+Mouse, Files, Connection — each with a specific tooltip explaining exactly *why* it is dimmed (no accessibility permission, controller role off, emergency stop active, peer offline, etc.). Sort is stable: connected+trusted first, then connected+untrusted, then discovered; alphabetical by name, UUID as a tiebreaker.
